body.x: Keeping watch over someone at risk of falling usually means a camera, which brings privacy concerns and depends on the lighting in the room. A fall can also happen at night, when watching matters just as much.

Cygbot Co., Ltd., an R&D company in Dongan-gu, Anyang, Gyeonggi Province, is taking a different route. Led by CEO Hyunmin Lee, the company will exhibit at KES 2026, where it plans to show a real-time AI fall-prevention LiDAR system and a ToF RGB-D camera module.

Cygbot says it specializes in light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensors for robotics and in real-time AI-based fall-prevention LiDAR systems. Built on its proprietary solid-state LiDAR and time-of-flight (ToF) technologies, the company says it develops compact, lightweight sensors for obstacle detection, distance measurement and spatial perception in robots, and that they are used in autonomous mobile robots, service robots and humanoid robots.

The fall-prevention system is the product it is putting forward at the show. According to Cygbot, it combines ToF depth data with edge AI to analyze human movement and the risk of a fall in real time, without using cameras. The company says it also lets users review the situation before and after an incident, which it describes as making the monitoring more reliable. Cygbot says its key competitive advantages are privacy protection and stable detection day and night, regardless of lighting conditions.

The second exhibit is the ToF RGB-D camera module, which Cygbot says received a KES Innovation Award. The company describes it as an ultra-compact 3D vision sensor that combines ToF and RGB technologies to provide accurate depth data and color 3D information at the same time. It says the module is suited to spatial perception and object recognition and to a range of humanoid and robotic applications.

Cygbot says its goal at the exhibition is to explore technology partnerships, proof-of-concept (PoC) opportunities and new business collaborations. The company reports no exports or overseas targets, and no specific future plans or difficulties, at this stage.

Now in its 57th edition, KES 2026 is Korea Electronics Show, a trade exhibition organized by the Korea Electronics Association (KEA) and hosted by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. It takes place from Tuesday, Oct. 13, to Friday, Oct. 16, at COEX in Seoul. Under the theme "AI in Motion," the show spans electronic parts and materials, AI transformation (AX), mobility solutions, robotics, digital health innovations, ESG sustainability, and Web3.0 and XR, with about 500 exhibitors and 70,000 visitors expected.
